text:
maria_support: customer (Acct: acme-inc) on Private/VPC deployment reports intermittent 502s and TLS handshake failures when traffic goes through their enterprise proxy. Issue started ~2024-08-27 18:30 UTC after they rotated node certs to ECDSA. They see request failures only from services that egress via the corp proxy, direct egress works fine. Repro steps from their side below.

maria_support: repro curl (fails):
```
curl -v https://private-controlplane.acme.internal/api/health --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080
* About to connect() to corp-proxy port 8080
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to private-controlplane.acme.internal:443
* CONNECT private-controlplane.acme.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
> CONNECT private-controlplane.acme.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1): handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) Received HTTP code 502 from proxy after CONNECT
```

maria_support: openssl s_client from a host behind the proxy (the proxy does TLS termination with upstream):
```
openssl s_client -connect private-controlplane.acme.internal:443 -servername private-controlplane.acme.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
140351234567616:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol:s23_clnt.c:794:
---
No peer certificate available
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 7 bytes and written 312 bytes
---
```

and the proxy logs show TLS alert 40 (handshake_failure) with a note: "no mutually-supported signature algorithm".

andrew_sre: can you get a full openssl -msg trace or the proxy handshake capture? usually this looks like a sig alg mismatch. what ciphers/signature algos does the control plane present?

maria_support: attached proxy TLS debug (excerpt):
```
Proxy TLS ClientHello -> supported_sig_algs: ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256, rsa_pss_rsae_sha256, rsa_pkcs1_sha256
Proxy upstream ServerHello -> accepted_sig_alg: rsa_pkcs1_sha256
Proxy log: "upstream cert sig alg rsa_pkcs1_sha256 not compatible with backend key (ecdsa)"
```

corp_net_admin: confirming: our corporate inline proxy (vendor: BlueGate) terminates client TLS and establishes a separate TLS session to upstream servers. Policy enforces upstream cert verification and we only allow RSA-signed server certs for legacy inspection modules. TLS1.3 is disabled on the proxy (we only negotiate TLS1.2). Allowed cipher suites list (excerpt):
```
TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256
TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
```

devon_eng: thanks, that explains it — the customer's control plane nodes are serving ECDSA leaf certs (ECDSA sig alg). The proxy only presents RSA-compatible sig algorithms upstream, and, because it performs TLS termination, it refuses to establish an upstream session if the upstream server's cert signature algorithm isn't in its allowed set. Result: proxy does not accept ECDSA-signed upstream certs -> handshake failure.

devon_eng: quick workarounds:
- short-term: re-issue or attach an RSA-signed cert on the control plane endpoint (or enable a dual-key certificate) so the proxy can complete the upstream handshake.
- medium: ask the corp proxy admins to add ECDSA signature algorithms to allowed list and enable TLS1.3 if possible.
- long-term: document recommended cert options for Private deployments so customers know to support environments that terminate TLS midstream.

andrew_sre: repro tip for their network team to validate locally: run openssl against the proxy's upstream session with -sigalgs and -tls1_2 to see what the proxy will accept:
```
openssl s_client -connect proxy-upstream.example:443 -tls1_2 -msg -sigalgs rsa_pkcs1_sha256
```
They can also test by configuring the control plane to present an RSA cert temporarily and confirm green traffic.

maria_support: acme-inc applied a temporary mitigation: swapped in an RSA-signed cert (from their CA) to the control plane host and traffic immediately normalized. They still want a long-term plan so they don't have to use RSA forever.

corp_net_admin: we can add ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 to allowed_sig_algs but we need vendor confirmation that inspection modules won't break. I'll open a change request with BlueGate and share timeline.

devon_eng: action items:
- maria_support: confirm which control plane services were affected and whether any cert rotation automation needs update (Assigned to you).
- devex/docs: add a note to Private deployment docs about proxy termination compatibility and recommended certificate options (RSA fallback or ensure proxy supports ECDSA).
- corp_net_admin: share vendor ticket ID when available.

maria_support: noted. customer is happy with temporary RSA fix for now. marking this thread as monitored until vendor response. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-08-28T02:11:08Z #private-controlplane-config -> success :white_check_mark:

maria_support: thanks team — keeping open until corp_net_admin confirms vendor change or customer switches cert rotation. :thumbsup:
